facts.raw_span: New York Heart Association functional class IV symptoms
New York Heart Association functional class IV symptoms

concepts.why: Patient has a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy with decreased ejection fraction, elevated jugular venous pressure, and signs of volume overload, indicating acute decompensated heart failure.
Patient has low blood pressure, elevated jugular venous pressure, and signs of volume overload, indicating cardiogenic shock.
Patient has worsening shortness of breath and bilateral lung crackles on auscultation, indicating pulmonary edema.
Patient has a regular atrial tachycardia at cycle length 320ms, indicating atrial tachycardia.
Patient has elevated creatinine levels, indicating renal insufficiency.
Patient has a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy with decreased ejection fraction, indicating ischemic cardiomyopathy.

rationales.F01: History of ischemic cardiomyopathy increases the likelihood of acute decompensated heart failure and cardiogenic shock.
rationales.F02: Low ejection fraction is a strong indicator of heart failure and cardiomyopathy.
rationales.F04: Worsening shortness of breath is a common symptom of pulmonary edema and heart failure.
rationales.F05: New York Heart Association functional class IV symptoms indicate severe heart failure.
rationales.F07: Tachycardia is a common finding in atrial tachycardia and heart failure.
rationales.F09: Elevated jugular venous pressure is a sign of volume overload and heart failure.
rationales.F10: Bilateral lung crackles are a common finding in pulmonary edema.
rationales.F11: Prominent S3 on cardiac auscultation is a sign of heart failure.
rationales.F12: Decreased ejection fraction indicates worsening heart function and increases the likelihood of heart failure and cardiomyopathy.

frontier_selector.rationale: Patient's worsening shortness of breath, New York Heart Association functional class IV symptoms, elevated jugular venous pressure, and prominent S3 on cardiac auscultation are consistent with acute decompensated heart failure, which is further supported by the markedly elevated N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide and decreased ejection fraction.
